heard: A spacecraft grabbed so much asteroid it couldn't close its lid. On October 20, 2020, NASA touched down on the carbon-rich near-Earth asteroid Bennu. The probe used a burst of nitrogen gas to blow surface, dust directly into the sampler head. Large rocks immediately jammed the Mylar seal flap wide open. Onboard cameras watched in horror as precious flakes of the asteroid drifted into the vacuum of space. Fearing a total loss, mission control rushed to stow the container days early. When the capsule finally landed in Utah in 2023, scientists recovered 121.6 grams of material. That accidental excess held the essential chemical building blocks of life, proving a spacecraft grabbed so much asteroid.
